rules.quote:
make edits with `Edit`/`Write` against absolute paths under the main
  project root.
rules.rule: When working in a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<slug>`, make file edits with `Edit`/`Write` using absolute paths under the main project root, not the worktree path.

rules.quote:
Run the project's build tool (`cargo`, `go`, `npm`, …) and `git`
  commands against the main project path.
rules.rule: When working in a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<slug>`, run the project's build tools and `git` commands against the main project path, not the worktree path.

rules.quote: Do NOT switch branches in the worktree to try to commit there.
rules.rule: When working in a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<slug>`, never switch branches in the worktree to commit there.

rules.quote: Match the existing commit style in `git log`
rules.rule: When writing commit messages, match the existing commit style visible in `git log`.

rules.quote:
short conventional-commit
subject lines
rules.rule: Write commit subject lines in short conventional-commit format.

rules.quote:
no body when the subject says
enough.
rules.rule: Omit the commit body when the subject line already conveys enough information.

rules.quote: Subject: `<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>` under ~72 chars.
rules.rule: Format commit subject lines as `<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>`, keeping them under about 72 characters.

rules.quote: Type is usually `fix` / `feat` / `refactor` / `chore` / `docs`.
rules.rule: Use `fix`, `feat`, `refactor`, `chore`, or `docs` as the commit type, usually.

rules.quote:
Scope
  is the package name (`dice`, `tui`, `parse`, …) or `docs`.
rules.rule: Use the package name as the commit scope, or `docs` for documentation changes.

rules.quote:
Add a body only when the *why* isn't obvious from the subject
  (e.g., a subtle invariant, an opt-out, a multi-step migration).
rules.rule: Add a commit body only when the reason for the change isn't obvious from the subject line, such as for a subtle invariant, an opt-out, or a multi-step migration.

rules.quote:
Multi-line / multi-paragraph bodies are explicitly OK when the
  content warrants it
rules.rule: Use multi-line or multi-paragraph commit bodies when the content warrants it.

rules.quote:
Don't
  pad, but don't truncate either; write what the reviewer needs.
rules.rule: Do not pad commit bodies with filler, but do not truncate them either; include what the reviewer needs.

rules.quote: **Do NOT add the `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer.**
rules.rule: Do not add a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer to commits.

rules.quote: This applies even when the harness's own commit template suggests it.
rules.rule: Do not add the `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer even when the harness's commit template suggests it.

rules.quote: Use suffixed engine method names (RollOnce, RollN) — never bare Roll
rules.rule: Use the suffixed engine method names RollOnce and RollN for dice evaluation, never the bare Roll name.

rules.quote:
Don't introduce or rename
back to a bare `Roll` form.
rules.rule: Do not introduce or rename any dice-engine evaluation method to a bare `Roll` form.

rules.quote:
follow the same suffix
  convention: lead with the verb, then the cardinality / variant tag.
rules.rule: When adding new dice-engine evaluation entry points, follow the suffix convention: lead with the verb, then the cardinality or variant tag.

rules.quote:
surface the
  rename impact for embedded consumers, not just the in-tree CLI/TUI.
rules.rule: When proposing API changes that touch the dice-engine evaluation methods, surface the rename impact for embedded consumers, not just the in-tree CLI/TUI.

rules.quote: Don't quietly reintroduce `Roll` as an alias "for convenience"
rules.rule: Do not add a `Roll` alias to the dice-engine evaluation methods for convenience.

rules.quote:
make
targeted inline edits (`Edit` on the specific lines) rather than
rewriting the whole file with `Write`.
rules.rule: When updating an existing file (especially memory files), make targeted inline edits on the specific lines that need to change using Edit, rather than rewriting the whole file with Write.

rules.quote: Keep existing wording where it's still true;
rules.rule: When updating an existing file, keep existing wording that is still true.

rules.quote:
add or adjust only the
  lines that need it, even if that makes the file less tidy than a
  fresh rewrite would be.
rules.rule: When updating an existing file, add or adjust only the lines that need changing, even if the result is less tidy than a fresh rewrite would be.

rules.quote: Whole-file `Write` is fine for brand-new files.
rules.rule: Using a whole-file Write is permitted when creating brand-new files.

rules.quote: For multi-file regex rewrites use the `Edit` tool (UTF-8 safe) with
rules.rule: For multi-file regex rewrites, use the Edit tool, which is UTF-8 safe.

rules.quote: or use ripgrep + `sed` via WSL bash.
rules.rule: For multi-file regex rewrites, ripgrep plus sed run via WSL bash may be used as an alternative to the Edit tool.

rules.quote: Don't use PowerShell `Get-Content`/`Set-Content` for text replacement on source files.
rules.rule: Do not use PowerShell Get-Content/Set-Content for text replacement on source files.

rules.quote:
prefer the language's
  Unicode escape syntax (`\u00XX` / `\U000XXXXX` in Go) over pasting
  the literal character
rules.rule: When tests need non-ASCII literals, prefer the language's Unicode escape syntax (e.g., \u00XX, or \U000XXXXX in Go) over pasting the literal character.

rules.quote:
If PowerShell really is the only option, set
  `[Console]::InputEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding =
  [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()`
rules.rule: If PowerShell is the only option, set Console InputEncoding and OutputEncoding to a UTF8Encoding instance.

rules.quote:
use
  `[IO.File]::ReadAllText(path, [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new())` /
  `WriteAllText`
rules.rule: If PowerShell is the only option, read and write files with [IO.File]::ReadAllText and WriteAllText using a UTF8Encoding instance.

rules.quote: just use `Edit`.
rules.rule: Even when PowerShell is used, prefer the Edit tool for file text rewrites because PowerShell approaches are error-prone.

rules.quote: Don't try to fix drift by editing the hook
rules.rule: Do not try to fix drift by editing the pre-commit hook.

rules.quote: `--no-verify` is off-limits
rules.rule: Do not bypass the pre-commit hook with `--no-verify`.

rules.quote: fix the source-of-truth that the script is comparing against.
rules.rule: When the drift checker reports drift, fix the source of truth the script compares against instead of the hook.

rules.quote: confirm the script path exists before assuming real drift.
rules.rule: When a commit fails, confirm the drift checker script path exists before assuming real drift.

rules.quote: surface that to David
rules.rule: If the drift checker script or its venv is missing on a machine, tell David rather than working around it.

rules.quote: rather than disabling the hook silently.
rules.rule: Do not disable the pre-commit hook silently when its script or venv is missing.

rules.quote: To run it without committing (either OS): `git hook run pre-commit`.
rules.rule: To run the pre-commit hook without committing, use `git hook run pre-commit` on either OS.

rules.quote: A portable-hook fix belongs in `dev-manifest.json`
rules.rule: Make portable pre-commit hook fixes in `dev-manifest.json` in dev-tools.

rules.quote: editing `~/dev/templates/` directly won't reach the Windows machine.
rules.rule: Do not edit `~/dev/templates/` directly to fix the pre-commit hook.

rules.quote: then gets copied into each app's `.githooks/pre-commit`
rules.rule: After a portable hook fix is made in `dev-manifest.json`, copy it into each app's `.githooks/pre-commit`.

rules.quote: so set it on any new clone.
rules.rule: Set `core.hooksPath` on any new clone of the repo.

rules.quote: verify with `git hook run pre-commit` on Windows before porting.
rules.rule: Verify the Windows hook branch with `git hook run pre-commit` on Windows before porting it to other repos.

rules.quote: Memory canonical location: `.claude/memory/` in the **project repo**
rules.rule: Store memory files in `.claude/memory/` within the project repo, not in `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`.

rules.quote: Any new memory writes go to the project repo.
rules.rule: Write any new memory files to the project repo, never to the legacy userdir location.

rules.quote: Read `CLAUDE.md` (auto-loaded by harness on Claude sessions).
rules.rule: At session start, read `CLAUDE.md` in the project root.

rules.quote: Read `AGENTS.md` for project context.
rules.rule: At session start, read `AGENTS.md` in the project root for project context.

rules.quote: Read `.claude/memory/MEMORY.md` and skim file titles; load the ones
rules.rule: At session start, read `.claude/memory/MEMORY.md` and skim its file titles.

rules.quote:
load the ones
  relevant to the task.
rules.rule: Load only the memory files relevant to the current task.

rules.quote:
take shell and path cues from whichever one the session is
on
rules.rule: Take shell and path cues from whichever machine the current session is running on (Windows or macOS), not from a fixed assumption.

rules.quote:
Take the language and toolchain cues from the
project itself, not from assumptions.
rules.rule: Determine the programming language and toolchain from the project itself, not from assumptions.

rules.quote: He prefers small, tested slices over large feature drops.
rules.rule: Deliver work in small, tested slices rather than large feature drops.

rules.quote:
Honest
reporting (what worked, what didn't, what was skipped).
rules.rule: Report honestly on what worked, what didn't, and what was skipped.

rules.quote:
Initiative on
already-agreed plans without re-asking
rules.rule: Take initiative to carry out already-agreed plans without re-asking for confirmation.

rules.quote:
redirection when priorities
shift
rules.rule: Redirect work when the user's priorities shift.
